userEnteredValue.stringValue: The NCCER/Build Your Future contribution funds the same AGC Workforce Development scholarship represented at Master row 144. Awards are up to $1,000 per year and renewable for up to two years, subject to continuing enrollment and good standing (2.5 GPA or equivalent). Students including high school seniors may pursue approved accredited construction degrees, certificates, craft training or registered apprenticeships full- or part-time; U.S. citizenship or permanent residency is required. The 2026–27 application is closed and requires a fall 2026 class. Its June 1 deadline time conflicts between the form header and body; no time is accepted as settled. Students pursuing a four-year bachelor's degree must use the separate AGC Undergraduate Scholarship application rather than this Workforce Development program.

userEnteredValue.stringValue: AMVETS Veteran Scholarship Program2024 supports veterans, including Guard/Reserve, active-duty service members or their spouses entering eligible construction-trades study. A high-school diploma or GED and eligible enrollment/acceptance are required; children are explicitly ineligible. Submit the named official Kaleidoscope application with eligibility verification, enrollment/acceptance and short essay. Awards range1000–5000. The verified route is the closed2024 program; the saved row’s2025label is not supported by that page and is retained as historical source provenance. userEnteredValue.stringValue: Montana STEM/Healthcare Scholarship Program is for Montana residents applying in the year they graduate from a high school accredited by the Montana Board of Public Education. It requires at least a 3.25 cumulative high-school GPA, four years of college-prep math and three years of college-prep science. Students must be accepted at an eligible campus, declare a qualifying STEM or healthcare major, seek their first certificate, two-year or four-year degree, enroll in at least 12 credits each semester and begin in the fall immediately after graduation. Apply through AwardMontana by March 15 (cycle year not stated), with the seventh-semester transcript, acceptance proof and counselor-signed math/science certification. Awards are $1,000 in year one, $1,500 in years two and three and $2,000 in year four if continuing requirements are met; not every program necessarily lasts four years.

userEnteredValue.stringValue: Donald E. Pizzini Memorial Nurse Scholarships provide up to $2,500 for full-time or part-time accredited nursing degree or certificate study relevant to long-term care. Applicants must be US citizens or permanent residents, reside in Montana, plan to work or remain working in Montana long-term-care nursing, and be available for a qualifying interview. A 3.0 prior GPA is required, using high-school GPA for first-year students; the committee may waive it for current long-term-care professionals based on work performance and experience. Acceptance or enrollment proof, official transcripts and two non-family recommendations are required. Preference goes to current long-term-care workers or those interested in that career, and people with current or past MHCA-member-facility employment. Use the official Initial Scholarship Application PDF for applicants who have not previously received this award. Applications are due the last day of February, with awards in April for the coming academic year; the year is unstated. Enrollment and continued participation must be proved for payments; the committee may withhold/cancel funds below3.0. Recipients may reapply after their award expires; renewal is not guaranteed.

Eligible institutions include UM, MSU and the named Montana affiliates. The page gives December 1–February 15 for seniors and December 1–March 1 for juniors; junior eligibility details and the next cycle year are not fully stated. Apply through Horatio Alger; an existing National Scholarship application is automatically considered. userEnteredValue.stringValue: MSU Hilleman Scholars is a program for Montana residents who are recent Montana high-school graduates with academic, leadership and career potential. The official application is labeled Fall 2026 without an exact deadline; the details page describes selection by invitation and still contains a 2025 orientation date. The program offers $4,000 per year for four years, conditional on academic progress and 10–15 hours each week of mentoring, learning, internship and community development activities. Completion of the Summer Success Academy is required to retain the offer, with a separate $2,000 academy stipend. The stated group study-abroad support is conditional. Hilleman cannot be stacked with Horatio Alger funding. Neither Pell eligibility nor first-generation status is established as a mandatory requirement by the checked public rules.

Applicants must reside in a Soroptimist International of the Americas member country or territory, including the United States; previous Women's Opportunity or Live Your Dream recipients, people with or pursuing a graduate degree, Soroptimist members, employees and their immediate family are ineligible. Applications run August 1–November 15 (cycle year not stated). Club awards vary; selected recipients may progress to regional and international levels, for a potential total of $1,000–$16,000.
